findings.message: `widgetViews` is declared but never initialised, so it is a nil map. The `widgetViews[id]++` on line 65 panics with "assignment to entry in nil map" on every request, and a panic in a handler also breaks CONTRIBUTING.md:9.

net/http serves each request on its own goroutine, so these unsynchronised writes to a package-level map are a data race. The Go runtime aborts the whole process with "concurrent map writes", which `recover` cannot catch. Guard the map with a `sync.Mutex`, or keep it on `Server` with a lock.

Any client-supplied int64 id adds a new map entry, without checking that the widget exists. A client can grow memory without bound by requesting many distinct ids, which is a cheap denial of service. Check the id against existing widgets before counting it.
